subject: Inference execution regions, subprocessor traceability, and deletion assurances - Q&A
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@finnovate.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@finnovate.com
Date: Thu, 9 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on where inference runs and deletion guarantees

Ben — thanks for the demo yesterday. A couple of procurement/security questions we need answered before we proceed to legal review. Can you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted API (and note differences for Dedicated/Private):

1) Exact regions where inference is executed (for requests that contain customer PII). Please list cloud regions and any transient hops.
2) A full list of subprocessors involved in request handling (compute, caching, logging, monitoring) and whether any subprocessor can access unencrypted request content.
3) Cross-border transfers: if a request originates in EU, can tokens or partial KV caches be sent to US-based GPUs or other regions? Under what conditions?
4) Deletion timelines and controls: how long request bodies, KV cache entries, and backups are retained? What options do we have to shorten these timelines?
5) Evidence: we need a short packet for our privacy team (SOC2 artifacts, regional processing map, and any contractual residency addenda).

We'd appreciate concise answers we can share with legal/procurement. If a technical owner should reply, point them here and we'll keep the thread open.

Thanks,
Alice Zhang
Head of Data Governance, Finnovate Health
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@finnovate.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Nov 2028 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on where inference runs and deletion guarantees

Alice — great questions, thanks. Below is a concise summary for procurement; Marissa (solutions) and Laura (contracts) are looped for detail and next steps. Short answers up-front, followed by bullets with specifics.

Short answers (hosted API / Dedicated / Private):
- Hosted API: primary execution in regional GPU pools (US-West, US-East, EU-West). We offer a regional routing commitment for paid accounts — but transient caching and autoscale burst capacity can route to a compatible region if the committed region is unavailable (we document fallbacks).
- Dedicated: guaranteed execution inside the customer's dedicated GPU pool in the nominated region(s); no cross-region routing unless explicitly enabled in the customer config.
- Private: customer-managed deployment (VPC/on-prem). Execution and all storage are in your network unless you opt into Redwood-managed telemetry; no Redwood cross-border transfers.

Bullet details:
1) Regions and hops:
- Compute: hosted inference executes on cloud VM/GPU instances in one of our supported regions: AWS us-west-2, AWS us-east-1, GCP europe-west1, and GCP europe-west4, and AP-SOUTHEAST-1 for APAC customers. Customers can request region pinning on paid plans.
- Transient hops: requests enter an API gateway regional ingress (nearest POP), then are routed to a region meeting the routing policy. When routing to a remote region occurs, only encrypted request payloads are forwarded; ephemeral KV cache shards (per-request prefixes) may be copied to the serving region for latency-sensitive reuse.

2) Subprocessors (summary):
- Cloud providers: AWS (EC2, S3 for ephemeral artifacts in some flows), GCP (Compute, Storage) — used strictly as compute and ephemeral object stores.
- CDN/edge: Fastly/Cloudflare for ingress throttling and DDoS protection (edge only, not storing request bodies).
- Observability: Datadog/Prometheus for metrics (does not receive unencrypted request content).
- Key management: AWS KMS / GCP KMS (we can integrate with customer KMS in Dedicated/Private).
- Third-party model infra: in some cases we use partner accelerators for optimized kernels; partners operate under subprocessor contracts and cannot access customer plaintext.

Access controls: subprocessors do not have access to plaintext request content unless explicitly configured (e.g., you enable Redwood-managed long-term storage or share unredacted logs). All inter-service transfers are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and sensitive payloads are encrypted at rest. We enforce least-privilege IAM roles on provider accounts.

3) Cross-border transfers:
- Hosted API default: if a request originates in the EU and your account is configured for EU residency, we will route to EU regions whenever capacity allows. However, under rare capacity events or for very short bursts, requests may be routed to a compatible non-EU region as part of our graceful fallback. When that happens, the transfer is logged and visible in the routing audit.
- Dedicated & Private: no cross-border transfers unless you enable multi-region replication.

4) Deletion timelines and options:
- Request bodies: by default, hosted API request bodies are retained for 30 days for debugging and QoS purposes, then deleted. Dedicated offers configurable retention; Private is under customer control.
- KV cache (prefix/KV): ephemeral cache entries live for the request lifetime + a short reuse window (default 1 hour). We can shorten that window on request or by policy for your account.
- Backups & snapshots: system snapshots (used for disaster recovery) are retained up to 90 days by default; we provide an option to reduce snapshot retention to 30 days under an enterprise addendum.
- Deletion mechanics: we provide automated erasure workflows and an API to request immediate purging of customer-specific artifacts; we publish an erasure token and a job id for audit tracking.

5) Evidence: attaching a short packet and a one-sheet. If procurement needs a formal residency addendum, Laura can attach contract language.

Attachments: redwood-regions-and-subprocessors-2028-11.pdf (summary), data-deletion-playbook.docx (playbook)

Next steps: Marissa — can you add a short technical note on KV cache scoping and share the internal routing audit sample? Laura — can you confirm the addendum template and whether we can offer 30-day snapshot retention for DF-4721?

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@finnovate.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Nov 2028 13:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on where inference runs and deletion guarantees

Hi Alice — quick tech addendum following Ben's summary. I put the most compliance-relevant points first.

Technical clarifications:
- KV cache sharding: KV cache is sharded per model instance and per-account namespace. Shards are ephemeral and only store compressed tensors/prefix keys; we do not persist raw prompt text unless caching is explicitly enabled. The default policy for hosted accounts stores only model-internal activations and short-lived prefix tokens (used for exact-match cache hits).
- Encryption: all cache shards are encrypted at rest with service-side keys. For Dedicated we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) so even in provider object stores only ciphertext exists without the CMK.
- Routing audit: we maintain a per-request trace id. If a request crosses regions, the audit shows source ingress POP, target compute region, timestamps, and the reason for cross-region routing (capacity/fallthrough). We can provide a sample audit for your legal review (anonymized).
- Deletion API semantics: immediate purge requests enqueue a job that deletes artifacts and then removes indices that reference them; full propagation across backups may take up to 72 hours in normal cases, 1-7 days in edge recovery cases unless you have the snapshot-retention addendum. We log the erasure job id and return a signed confirmation to the requester.

Operational options we can offer DF-4721:
- Residency SLA: EU-only execution with no cross-border fallback (requires Dedicated or Private and a small configuration premium).
- Short retention profile: change request-body retention to 0 days (no retention) and KV cache lifetime to 5 minutes for sensitive routes. This is possible for Dedicated and for hosted accounts under an enterprise plan.
- Auditing bundle: include a sample routing audit, subprocessor contracts redacted copy, and SOC2 evidence summary.

I can assemble the routing audit sample and a short runbook that describes the purge workflow. If you want, we can redact any customer-specific meta and ship it to procurement/legal.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alice — I reviewed the attached packet and had two quick contract points to surface:

1) Residency Addendum: We have a one-page residency addendum that disallows cross-border fallbacks for the duration of the contract. For hosted customers we can offer this for an enterprise commitment; Dedicated/Private customers already have the contractual control.
2) Deletion SLA: We can commit to a 30-day max snapshot retention or opt into a 30-day snapshot retention and accelerated purge (48-72 hour guaranteed propagation) as part of an enterprise security addendum.

I'll attach the two contract snippets and a DocuSign link if you want to add the residency addendum to your SOW: https://docusign.redwood.com/DF-4721/residency-addendum

If these options look acceptable, Ben — let's schedule a 30-min call with procurement/legal next week. Alice — what times are you available Tue/Wed PST?

Regards,
Laura Bennett
